_why: Nikola Tesla, everything published in his lifetime and before the 1931 US public-domain line (2026-09-25, Derek: 'and then tesla, we need everything'): the 1892 London/Paris lecture (English, and the 1894 German edition), Martin's 1894 Inventions Researches and Writings (already held), the Westinghouse 'Transmission of Power' patent collection, Century 1900 'Problem of Increasing Human Energy', the 1916–1919 Electrical Experimenter pieces (My Inventions, The True Wireless, Telautomatics, Egg of Columbus), the 1898 electrotherapy paper, Johnson's Songs of Liberty (Tesla co-translated the Zmaj poems), and every individual patent scan. OUT: post-1930 editions and compilations (Colorado Springs Notes 1978, Complete Patents 1979/1994, Leland Anderson's 1992 edition, 'Tesla Papers', 'Very Truly Yours'), the Czechoslovak electronics firm TESLA's manuals, Tesla Inc., arXiv authors named Tesla, and the 'Tesla Leila Kh' self-publications.
